question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & 1 & 4\\5 & 6 & 0\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Find the cofactor matrix of $A$.

(b) Hence, obtain $\operatorname{adj}A$ and evaluate $|A|$.

(c) Determine $A^{-1}$ and verify that $AA^{-1}=I$.
explanation:
(a)
The cofactors are
$$A_{11}=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 4\\6 & 0\end{vmatrix}=-24,\quad A_{12}=-\begin{vmatrix}0 & 4\\5 & 0\end{vmatrix}=20,\quad A_{13}=\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1\\5 & 6\end{vmatrix}=-5$$
$$A_{21}=-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\6 & 0\end{vmatrix}=18,\quad A_{22}=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3\\5 & 0\end{vmatrix}=-15,\quad A_{23}=-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\5 & 6\end{vmatrix}=4$$
$$A_{31}=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\1 & 4\end{vmatrix}=5,\quad A_{32}=-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3\\0 & 4\end{vmatrix}=-4,\quad A_{33}=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\0 & 1\end{vmatrix}=1$$
Therefore, the cofactor matrix is
$$C=\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 20 & -5\\18 & -15 & 4\\5 & -4 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix:
$$\operatorname{adj}A=C^T=\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 18 & 5\\20 & -15 & -4\\-5 & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Expanding $|A|$ along the first row using its cofactors,
$$|A|=1(-24)+2(20)+3(-5)=-24+40-15=1$$

(c)
Since $|A|=1\neq0$,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 18 & 5\\20 & -15 & -4\\-5 & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$AA^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & 1 & 4\\5 & 6 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 18 & 5\\20 & -15 & -4\\-5 & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\0 & 1 & 0\\0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=I$$
Hence, the inverse is verified.
